title: Canva releases its first image generation model
slides: Canva's new AI model threatens graphic designers' jobs?
It generates images directly inside the design editor
But trained on Canva's own licensed assets, not scraped art
Users can now create original visuals without stock photos
Test one image today and judge the quality yourself
thread_text:
1. Designers, worried yet?

Canva now generates images directly inside its editor, no plugins needed. Your workflow might never be the same.

2. How it was trained

Unlike other AI art tools, Canva's model learned only from its own licensed assets—no scraped art. That could mean fewer copyright headaches.

3. Create without stock photos

Users can now generate original visuals on the spot, ditching generic stock images. Brands get unique content instantly.

4. The quality test

Canva invites you to try one image today and judge the results yourself. The real question is whether it meets your standards.

5. Try it on your next post

Generate one image in Canva and compare it to your usual stock photo. Does it save time or create extra editing work? Test it this week.

instagram.caption:
Canva now generates images inside its design editor, no plugins, no stock photo tabs.

Its model was trained only on Canva's own licensed assets, not scraped art—which means fewer copyright headaches for the visuals you publish.

You can type a prompt and get an original image on the spot, ready for your next post. 🎨

That changes the workflow: fewer generic stock photos, but also a new question—will the output actually meet your standards, or create extra editing work? 🧐

Try one image in Canva this week and compare it to your usual stock photo. Does it save time or cost you more? ⏱️
